questions.question: Which pair is congruent modulo 5?
questions.explanation: 17 − (−3) = 20, a multiple of 5, so 17 ≡ −3 (mod 5). Both leave remainder 2. The other differences, −16, −4 and 12, are not multiples of 5.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to conclude x ≡ 1 (mod 6) from 3x ≡ 3 (mod 6)?
options: Because gcd(3, 6) = 3, so 3 has no inverse mod 6; for example x = 3 also works
Because 6 is too small a modulus
questions.explanation: Cancelling means multiplying by an inverse, and 3 has one mod 6 only if gcd(3, 6) = 1. It is 3, and indeed 3·3 = 9 ≡ 3 although 3 ≢ 1.

questions.question: If a ≡ b (mod n), which statement is NOT guaranteed?
options: aᶜ ≡ bᶜ (mod n) for positive c
questions.explanation: Bases can be replaced but exponents cannot. For example 1 ≡ 6 (mod 5), but (−1)¹ = −1 and (−1)⁶ = 1 are not congruent mod 5.
